es.summary: Proceso de información y apoyo para personas con riesgo o diagnóstico de trastornos genéticos, orientado a la toma de decisiones informada.
key_points: Definición: interacción educativa y de apoyo sobre riesgos genéticos.
Indicaciones: historial familiar, embarazo >35 años, pérdida recurrente de embarazos, anomalías en pruebas prenatales.
Rol de la enfermera: recopilar historia, explicar pruebas, facilitar decisiones y referir al genetista.
Aspectos éticos y legales: confidencialidad, consentimiento informado y no discriminación.
Comunicación: lenguaje claro, sensibilidad cultural y apoyo emocional.

purpose: Brindar información clara sobre riesgos genéticos.
Apoyar emocionalmente al paciente y familia.
Facilitar la toma de decisiones informada.
procedure: Obtener historia familiar y personal de trastornos genéticos.
Evaluar factores de riesgo (edad materna, pérdidas previas, resultados de cribado).
Explicar tipos de pruebas genéticas y sus implicaciones.
Discutir opciones de manejo, prevención y planificación familiar.
Derivar al genetista o laboratorio especializado.
Programar seguimiento para revisar resultados y decisiones.
safety: Garantizar confidencialidad de la información genética.
Obtener consentimiento informado antes de cualquier prueba.
Respetar valores culturales y creencias del paciente.
Evitar sesgos y discriminación por resultados genéticos.
nursing_care: Evaluar nivel de conocimiento y ansiedad antes de la sesión.
Proveer material educativo adaptado al nivel de comprensión.
Observar reacciones emocionales y ofrecer apoyo psicológico.
Reportar cualquier angustia significativa al equipo de salud.
Reforzar la comprensión mediante preguntas de retroalimentación.
documentation: Fecha y hora de la sesión de asesoramiento.
Motivo de la consulta y antecedentes familiares relevantes.
Información proporcionada y preguntas del paciente.
Decisiones tomadas y plan de pruebas o derivaciones.
Evaluación de comprensión y plan de seguimiento.

evidenced_by: expresión de incertidumbre sobre riesgo genético
outcomes: Conocimiento del riesgo genético: 80% de respuestas correctas en entrevista de seguimiento
Participación en pruebas genéticas recomendadas: 100% según plan de cuidados

interventions.action: Recopilar y registrar historia familiar y personal de trastornos genéticos.
interventions.rationale: Identifica factores de riesgo que guían la educación y las pruebas.

interventions.action: Proveer información escrita y verbal sobre el trastorno, pruebas disponibles y opciones de manejo.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la comprensión y reduce la incertidumbre.

interventions.action: Utilizar técnicas de enseñanza activa (preguntas abiertas, retroalimentación) para evaluar comprensión.
interventions.rationale: Permite confirmar que el paciente ha internalizado la información.

interventions.action: Derivar al paciente al genetista clínico para evaluación y pruebas específicas.
interventions.rationale: Asegura acceso a pruebas especializadas y asesoramiento adicional.

interventions.action: Documentar la sesión, preguntas del paciente y plan de pruebas en el registro de salud.
interventions.rationale: Mantiene continuidad del cuidado y facilita la comunicación interprofesional.

en.summary: Process of information and support for individuals at risk or diagnosed with genetic disorders, aimed at informed decision-making.
key_points: Definition: educational and supportive interaction about genetic risks.
Indications: family history, pregnancy >35 years, recurrent pregnancy loss, anomalies in prenatal tests.
Nurse role: collect history, explain tests, facilitate decisions and refer to geneticist.
Ethical and legal aspects: confidentiality, informed consent and non-discrimination.
Communication: clear language, cultural sensitivity and emotional support.

purpose: Provide clear information about genetic risks.
Emotionally support the patient and family.
procedure: Obtain family and personal history of genetic disorders.
Assess risk factors (maternal age, prior losses, screening results).
Explain types of genetic tests and their implications.
Discuss management options, prevention and family planning.
Refer to geneticist or specialized laboratory.
Schedule follow-up to review results and decisions.
safety: Obtain informed consent before any test.
Respect cultural values and patient beliefs.
Avoid bias and discrimination based on genetic results.
nursing_care: Assess knowledge level and anxiety before the session.
Provide educational material adapted to comprehension level.
Observe emotional reactions and offer psychological support.
Report significant distress to the health team.
documentation: Date and time of counseling session.
Reason for visit and relevant family history.
Decisions made and plan for testing or referrals.
Assessment of understanding and follow-up plan.

evidenced_by: expression of uncertainty about genetic risk
outcomes: Knowledge of genetic risk: 80% correct responses in follow-up interview
Participation in recommended genetic tests: 100% per care plan

interventions.action: Collect and record family and personal history of genetic disorders.
interventions.rationale: Identifies risk factors that guide education and testing.

interventions.action: Provide written and verbal information about the disorder, available tests and management options.
Use active teaching techniques (open questions, feedback) to assess comprehension.
interventions.rationale: Allows confirmation that the patient has internalized the information.

interventions.action: Refer the patient to a clinical geneticist for evaluation and specific tests.
interventions.rationale: Ensures access to specialized testing and additional counseling.

interventions.action: Document the session, patient questions and testing plan in the health record.
interventions.rationale: Maintains continuity of care and facilitates interprofessional communication.

key_points.1.quote: You may consider it if you : Have a personal or family history of a genetic condition or birth defect Are pregnant or planning to be pregnant after age 35 Already have a child with a genetic disorder or birth defect Have had two or more pregnancy losses or a baby who died Have had ultrasound or screening tests that suggest a possible problem

key_points.3.quote: The ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI) associated with advances in genetic and genomic knowledge include informed decision-making, informed consent for genetic testing, consent related to genetic/genomic research, privacy and confidentiality, and discrimination prevention (Soleymani-Lehmann et al., 2022).

sections.purpose.0.quote: Provide the patient and family with information about testing, the types of tests, benefits or risks, and the reasons testing is needed.

sections.purpose.1.quote: Genetic counseling provides information and support to people who have, or may be at risk for, genetic disorders .

sections.purpose.2.quote: Genetic carrier screening identifies the risk for having a child with inherited disorders, such as cystic fibrosis or Tay-Sachs disease , and promotes informed decision-making regarding reproductive options (Montgomery, 2021).

sections.purpose.3.quote: If the history reveals red flags related to risk for inherited disorders, a referral for genetic counseling is indicated.

sections.procedure.2.quote: Types of genetic testing include single-gene testing, panel testing, and large-scale genetic testing.

sections.procedure.5.quote: After testing, nurses are responsible for following up with patients to communicate test results.

sections.safety.0.quote: Maintaining privacy and confidentiality regarding genetic health information has the potential for presenting complex concerns for nursing practice.

sections.safety.1.quote: Genetic testing procedures also require assuring that the patient clearly understands the purposes, benefits, and risks involved with testing, facilitating informed decision-making and consent (Soleymani-Lehmann et al., 2022).

sections.safety.2.quote: Cultural beliefs and practices influence uptake of information and understanding of genetic disease.

sections.safety.3.quote: The Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA) prohibits discrimination based on genetic information in both areas.

sections.documentation.1.quote: You may consider it if you : Have a personal or family history of a genetic condition or birth defect

sections.documentation.2.quote: Nurses serve as educators, providing patients with comprehensive information about genetic testing, including its purpose, potential benefits, limitations, and implications for health management, as well as preparing and assisting patients during the testing process.

sections.documentation.3.quote: If the history reveals red flags related to risk for inherited disorders, a referral for genetic counseling is indicated.

sections.documentation.4.quote: They ensure that patients clearly understand the testing process, its potential outcomes, and any associated risks or ethical considerations.
